newsitem.title: USA: Man dies after Bronco flips off Mackinac Bridge.
newsitem.headline: Man dies after Bronco flips off Mackinac Bridge.

text.p: Weather did not appear to be a factor in a Ford Bronco's flipping over the Mackinac Bridge guard rail and through the ice 200 feet below, police said Monday.

Searchers from a U.S. Coast Guard helicopter recovered the body of Richard Alan Daraban, 25, of Utica, Mich., from the ice underneath the bridge after the accident, which occurred about 6:30 p.m. Sunday, authorities said.
Built in 1957, the Mackinac Bridge separates the upper and lower peninsulas of Michigan and is the longest suspension bridge in the world.
On Monday, a poice spokesman said weather did not appear to play a role in Sunday's accident. "The road was dry and the winds were light at the time," said Michigan State Police Sgt. Kenneth Hardy.

The leased 1996 Bronco was travelling southbound in the left lane of the bridge. After passing a tractor trailer rig, the Bronco swerved back into the right lane, struck the guard rail and careened off the bridge.

It was the second such fatal accident in the bridge's 40-year history. On Sept. 22, 1989, Leslie Pluhar of Royal Oak, Mich., died when her Yugo, a small, light-weight car, hit the guard rail in high winds and fell over the side. She was the first person to die in a car that crashed off the bridge.
